chapter: New York 1936-39 (second pass of the transcript)
title: Early bass inspirations and no jamming in Philadelphia (second pass)
summary: Hall again names Kirby and Taylor and says jamming did not happen until New York.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: players who you, you know, favored and who you were inspired by?
Not yet. I was always inspired by John Kirby and Billy Taylor and the Duke.
Well, he's -- when I started playing bass these are the people that I heard.
Did you hear Kirby when he was with Fletcher Henderson?

No, I didn't hear him when he was with Fletcher Henderson, but I -- he used to come to Philadelphia. He was with Fletcher Henderson but we didn't, I didn't get a chance to go hear the band because we were playing at a club or something but he, wherever I was playing, after they finished you know, the musicians, they'd come from New York. And I was working in some little joint in Philly.
Now, you mentioned when Ellington or Calloway used to come there was no sitting in, but how about these other kinds of places. Was there jamming and sitting in, did you get a chance to --
No. The jamming didn't happen until New York. They were finished with what they had to do.
And they just came to relax and listen.
